Practices.Summary: Google operates TAP (Test Automation Platform), a massive continuous build system that handles the entire codebase, responsible for running automated tests before and after code submission, handling over 50,000 unique changes daily with more than four billion test cases executed.

evidence.quote: We run a massive continuous build, called the Test Automation Platform (TAP), of our entire codebase.
Every day it is responsible for handling more than 50,000 unique changes and running more than four billion individual test cases.

Practices.Summary: Google's CI follows a two-tier testing strategy: fast, reliable small tests run on presubmit to catch issues before submission, while comprehensive test suites run on post-submit to validate integrated changes, balancing speed with coverage.

evidence.quote: Most teams at Google run their small tests (like unit tests) on presubmit—these are the obvious ones to run as they tend to be the fastest and most reliable.
our general rule of thumb is: only fast, reliable ones. You can accept some loss of coverage on presubmit, but that means you need to catch any issues that slip by on post-submit

Practices.Summary: Continuous Delivery at Google assembles release candidates (RCs) from code, configuration, and dependencies that passed the continuous build, then promotes and tests these candidates through a series of environments before reaching production.

evidence.quote: Release candidate (RC): A cohesive, deployable unit created by an automated process, assembled of code, configuration, and other dependencies that have passed the continuous build.

Continuous Delivery (CD): a continuous assembling of release candidates, followed by the promotion and testing of those candidates throughout a series of environments—sometimes reaching production and sometimes not.

Practices.Summary: Each team has a designated Build Cop whose responsibility is keeping all tests passing in their project regardless of who breaks them, with rapid rollback capability allowing any change to be rolled back with two clicks to quickly restore broken builds.

evidence.quote: To deal with such breakages, each team has a 'Build Cop.' The Build Cop's responsibility is keeping all the tests passing in their particular project, regardless of who breaks them.
Any change to Google's codebase can be rolled back with two clicks!

Practices.Summary: Static configuration at Google is version controlled alongside code and goes through the same code review process, ensuring configuration changes are tested along with corresponding code as part of release candidates to prevent configuration bugs.

evidence.quote: at Google, static configuration is in version control along with the code, and hence goes through the same code review process.
any static configuration you do have should be promoted as part of the release candidate so that it can undergo testing along with its corresponding code.

Practices.Summary: Google's Continuous Build integrates the latest code changes at head and runs automated build and test, with most teams cutting release candidates at green (latest validated) head rather than true (latest committed) head for stability.

evidence.quote: The Continuous Build (CB) integrates the latest code changes at head and runs an automated build and test.
At Google, most teams cut these at green, as opposed to true, head.

Issues.Issue_Title: run_live() silently terminates on max_llm_calls exhaustion — no event, no exception, no resumption path
Issues.Description: Live agent session terminates silently when hitting max_llm_calls limit without emitting termination event or raising exception, blocking proper error handling and session recovery

Issues.Issue_Title: deps: pinned litellm <=1.82.6 has 5 active CVEs (2 critical) -- upstream fix in litellm 1.83.7
Issues.Description: Pinned dependency on litellm version 1.82.6 exposes ADK to 5 active security vulnerabilities including 2 critical CVEs, requiring urgent dependency upgrade to 1.83.7

Issues.Issue_Title: to_a2a(Workflow) fails when Workflow contains LlmAgent with input_schema/output_schema (ADK 2.0.0b1)
Issues.Description: Workflow serialization to A2A format fails when LlmAgent includes input/output schema definitions in ADK 2.0 beta, blocking schema-validated agent workflows

Issues.Issue_Title: Windows: file:///C:/... artifact URIs are resolved to the wrong filesystem path
Issues.Description: Platform-specific URI parsing bug on Windows where file:///C:/... URIs are incorrectly resolved to wrong filesystem paths, breaking artifact storage and retrieval

Issues.Issue_Title: AgentTool.run_async extracts only p.text, loses code_execution_result.output from inner code-executor agents
Issues.Description: Nested agent tool execution discards code execution results by only extracting text parts, losing structured output from inner code-executor agents

Issues.Issue_Title: AgentEngineSandboxCodeExecutor: external-delete recovery catches wrong exception class (genai.ClientError vs api_core.NotFound)
Issues.Description: Exception handling bug in sandbox code executor where recovery code catches genai.ClientError instead of api_core.NotFound, causing unhandled exceptions during cleanup

Issues.Issue_Title: ApiRegistry doesn't work for newly enabled services
Issues.Description: MCP tool ApiRegistry fails to discover newly enabled Google Cloud services, requiring registry refresh or restart to detect service availability changes

Issues.Issue_Title: tool_trajectory_avg_score returns 0.0 even when tool name and args match exactly
Issues.Description: Evaluation metric tool_trajectory_avg_score incorrectly returns 0.0 score despite perfect tool name and argument matches, indicating evaluation framework scoring bug

Issues.Issue_Title: adk deploy agent_engine fails on custom project structures due to hardcoded '.agent' import
Issues.Description: Deployment command hardcodes '.agent' import path, breaking deployments for custom project structures that don't follow default ADK scaffolding conventions
Code execution sandbox fails with MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL errors when using Gemini 2.x models due to incompatible function calling format changes between model versions

Practices.Summary: From the 10 issues analyzed, common engineering pitfalls include: (1) dependency security vulnerabilities (CVEs in litellm), (2) platform-specific path handling bugs (Windows file URI resolution), (3) model version compatibility breaks (Gemini 2.x sandbox executor), (4) evaluation framework scoring bugs (tool_trajectory metrics), (5) exception handling mismatches (wrong exception types caught), (6) hardcoded assumptions breaking custom setups (deployment import paths), and (7) silent failure modes (live session termination). ADK tracks public bugs on google/adk-python GitHub issues while Vertex AI components use Google Issue Tracker.
